newsitem.title: USA: NATIONAL WESTERN LIFE CPA AFFIRMED - S&P.
newsitem.headline: NATIONAL WESTERN LIFE CPA AFFIRMED - S&P.

text.p: NEW YORK, June 27 - Standard & Poor's today has affirmed its single-'A'-plus claims-paying ability rating of National Western Life Insurance Co. (NWL).

The rating reflects the company's superior capitalization, strong earnings, excellent liquidity, and good asset quality. These strengths are partially offset by an overall business profile that is considered adequate and the ultimate cost related to litigation associated with its Westcap subsidiary.
-- NWL's key strength is superior capitalization, with a Standard & Poor's capital adequacy ratio of 271% at year-end 1996.
-- Earnings have been very strong, with return on assets (ROA) averaging over 155 basis points (bp) over the past five years.
-- Liquidity is excellent. The portfolio consists of readily marketable investments of high credit quality.

--NWL's asset quality is good, with bonds representing over 80% of invested assets. Below investment-grade bonds represent less than 0.5%. Mortgage loans, equity securities, and real estate account for less than 10% of invested assets.

-- NWL's business profile is considered adequate, and it has a favorable niche in the life insurance market in Latin America. Universal life in the international arena have remained relatively flat. Domestic life premiums were down about 3% in 1996. Total premiums in 1996 were down about 9% from 1995.

-- The company's ultimate cost associated with Westcap's litigation is not known presently. In March 1997, NWL made a $1 million cash infusion to Westcap for operational expenses incurred during Westcap's Chapter 11 reorganization. That cash infusion will be credited against any future settlement or litigation recovery related to Westcap's alleged claims against NWL.
-- ROA will be in excess of 120 bp.
-- International life sales will grow at 3%-5% per year. Friday, 27 June 1997 21:34:29 ENDS nN27632623
